title: Structuralism: signs, binary oppositions and Propp's folktale functions
examples: What is the difference between signifier and signified?

explain.say: Look at the letters c, a, t. There is nothing cat-like about them. The linguist Ferdinand de Saussure noticed this, and his students published his lectures in 1916. On the board: a sign has two halves, the signifier, the sound or marks, and the signified, the idea.

draw.text: Structuralism: signs, binary oppositions and Propp's folktale functions

explain.say: See the left side? The link is arbitrary: Spanish says gato, Hindi says billi, Japanese says neko. And a word means by difference: cat is cat because it is not bat, cut or dog. Structuralists say meaning comes from the whole system, not from things. Can you name another word that only works by contrast?

The anthropologist Claude Levi-Strauss found that myths are built on opposite pairs. Look at Little Red Riding Hood sorted on the board: the village and the path on the side of culture, the forest and the wolf on the side of nature. The story happens when she strays across the line. Which pair drives your favourite story?

explain.say: In 1928 Vladimir Propp studied a hundred Russian fairy tales and found thirty-one functions, always in the same order, and seven roles like hero, villain and donor. Here is a short version of his chain. Watch the donor test the hero. Does a superhero film follow this?

explain.say: So structuralism looks for the hidden grammar under all stories, the way grammar sits under every sentence. Critics later said it ignored history and the single, surprising text, which led to post-structuralism. Well done. Challenge: map the last film you watched onto Propp's chain, from lack to wedding.

faq.q: What is a signifier and a signified?
faq.a: In Saussure's model a sign has two sides: the signifier is the sound or written form, and the signified is the concept it calls up. Together they make the sign.
Because nothing in the sound or letters naturally connects to the idea. Different languages use completely different words for the same concept.
asks: What does arbitrary mean in Saussure?

faq.a: Pairs of opposites, like culture and nature or light and dark, that structuralists see as the hidden frame of myths and stories.
asks: What is a binary opposition in literature?

faq.a: Propp identified thirty-one typical actions, such as villainy, departure, the donor's test and the wedding, that appear in the same order in Russian fairy tales.

faq.q: Who is the donor in a folktale?
faq.a: In Propp's scheme the donor tests the hero, then gives a magic object or helper that makes victory possible, like the fairy godmother in Cinderella.
asks: What is a donor in Propp?

facts: Saussure's Course in General Linguistics was published in 1916, three years after his death, from students' notes.
Propp's Morphology of the Folktale (1928) analysed 100 Russian fairy tales.
Propp named seven character roles, including hero, villain, donor, helper and false hero.
